brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 girls' birthday evites (unicorns, princess castles, mermaids, fairy gardens, butterflies, ballet, cupcakes, rainbows, kittens, art studio, carousel, pop star), several with scratch-and-reveal. Push past the pink-and-glitter default without losing what kids actually love.
brief.audience: Parents of 3 to 10 year olds; the kids are the first viewers.
brief.feeling: Enchantment with real craft; delight that feels hand-made.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.
references: Exploration grid A: pastel 3D baby unicorns on cotton-candy clouds with balloons, a crescent-moon nap, a rainbow; very sweet, very pink.
Exploration grid B: luminous underwater kingdoms, coral, jellyfish, an open shell with pearls, god-rays through turquoise water; no characters.

proposals.title: The Illuminated Folio
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single page from a hand-ruled medieval illuminated manuscript — the child's party is the text, the magic is the marginalia come to life.
proposals.geometry: A strict 4:5 portrait ratio governed by the Van de Graaf canon: a text block occupying 4/9 of the page width, flanked by proportional margins that widen toward the outer edge. A ruling baseline grid of 12 equal horizontal bands anchors all type and ornament — the same count as a Book of Hours gathering. Decorative borders are set within the outer margin column, never bleeding into the text block. Every evite uses this identical skeleton; the theme changes what inhabits the cells, not the measure itself.
proposals.typography: Primary display in IM Fell English (Google Fonts, open licence) at 28–34px, set in Title Case with tracked small-caps for the child's name — the capitals are sized to one full baseline unit, so they sit like a drop cap inside the text block. Secondary information (date, venue) in Cormorant Garamond Regular at 14px, letterspaced +40. No sans-serif anywhere. All type is live in Tela; name and date fields are styled identically across all 12 so a parent sees the same editorial register no matter which theme. The folio number — the evite's serial ornament — appears bottom-right in 10px italic, baseline-aligned to the last ruling line.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. The art plate is a single hand-painted gouache illustration per theme — unicorn, mermaid, etc. — executed in the flat, jewel-toned style of a 13th-century English psalter (think the Rutland Psalter marginalia, transformed: no heraldic content, wholly original characters). Each painting is scanned at 1200dpi, then colour-separated into 3 layers: the ground wash, the mid-tone figural drawing, and the gold-ink line work. The gold layer is replaced at render time by the WebGL foil-shimmer mask so the gilding is live and responsive to light. The scratch-and-reveal mechanic exposes a hidden sub-scene painted in the same hand beneath the border ornament — the kitten behind the floral tracery, the mermaid beneath a lattice of sea-glass — so the reveal feels like uncovering an existing thing, not generating a new one.
proposals.texture: Vellum tooth. The ground plate carries a photographed sheet of real calfskin vellum (Plajah-owned scan, not stock) used as a multiply-blend texture layer — it reads as warmth and slight grain, never as a filter. Border ornaments are inked on the same vellum scan so the texture is continuous, not composited. The WebGL bokeh layer sits above all of this; its particles are shaped as tiny heraldic lozenges, not circles, keeping the system coherent.
proposals.motion: The tilt-reactive foreground cut-outs are the marginalia figures — the unicorn, the butterfly, the carousel horse — which drift at parallax depth 0.6× relative to the text block. The text block itself does not move; it is the fixed measure. On load, the gold foil shimmer rakes across the ruling lines from top-left to bottom-right in 1.4 seconds, like a page turning toward a window — this is the entrance. The scratch-and-reveal border activates on a slow finger-drag across the outer margin only; the interior text block is never disturbed. Candle-flicker particles (for Birthday evites using the carousel and cupcake themes) pulse at 0.8Hz, a rate measured from an actual filmed candle, not a sine wave default. Reduced-motion mode: the rake shimmer becomes a single static foil state; parallax depth drops to 0.1×; particles freeze.
proposals.productionMethod: Each of the 12 gouache paintings is made physically on 300gsm hot-press paper with Schmincke Horadam paints, then scanned. The vellum texture is a Plajah-owned archival scan. Vector border tracery is drawn in Affinity Designer over a photographed ruling-pen line (the ruling pen leaves a slight ink-bead at the stroke end that survives vectorisation as a node — this is the human trace at the vector level). The three image layers are exported as WebP at 60% quality; the gold layer is a single-channel PNG mask handed to the WebGL foil shader. All type is live. Total art-plate payload targets under 280kb per evite.
proposals.humanTrace: The ruling-pen ink bead at the end of every border stroke — visible at 2× zoom as a slight swell in the line weight, preserved through the vectorisation because it was drawn, not constructed. The vellum scan carries the faint ghost of a previous page's text showing through the skin. Both are perceptible without explanation.
proposals.risk: Parents may read 'medieval' as cold, ecclesiastical, or inaccessible for a 4-year-old's birthday. The risk is worth taking because the illuminated manuscript is one of the oldest recorded forms of decorated, story-holding, hand-made beauty — children respond to intricate miniature worlds before they read genre, and the craft legibility (the gold, the fine line, the hidden scene) does the emotional work that pink glitter currently does by volume rather than by quality. The measure holds the enchantment; the enchantment earns the measure.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a swell, a burst, a moment that declares its own arrival. I want the scratch mechanic to uncover something that was always there, silent, as if the border always held it. The disagreement is whether surprise requires spectacle. I say the sub-scene has more power if it does not perform its own disclosure; the Dramatist will say I am wi

proposals.title: Ink First, Screen Second
proposals.idea: Each evite begins as a hand-pulled linocut or woodblock print — carved, inked, pressed, scanned at full damage — and the WebGL layer acts as varnish poured over the physical dent, not decoration laid on top of nothing.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile column; a single bleed-edge block print occupies the full plate with no margin — the carved image runs off all four sides the way a real print does when you over-ink; live text sits in a 32px-guttered safe zone punched out of the print's own negative space, not floated over it; foreground cut-outs break the boundary of that safe zone by 8–12px on one edge only, giving asymmetric life without chaos
proposals.typography: Display: Playfair Display in an extra-heavy optical size, letterspaced at -0.02em, set in ALL CAPS but with the first letter dropped one baseline below the rest — not a drop cap, a stumble, intentional; body/detail text: iA Writer Quattro Mono at 13px, tracking 0.08em, because it reads like someone typed the party details on a real machine; NO rounded sans, no bubble letters — the kids are smarter than that
proposals.imageLogic: Each theme is a hand-carved linocut block — unicorn horn = gouge marks visible; mermaid tail = cross-hatched scales in relief; ballet tutu = concentric ring cuts — photographed under raking studio light to show ink relief and paper emboss before any digital touch; then scanned at 1200dpi; the scan becomes the art plate; color is applied digitally only as a single flat flood behind the carved white negative, so the cut itself is always the image
proposals.texture: Lino surface grain reads through the ink; ink drag at the edges of each stroke is preserved; paper emboss shows as a subtle height map fed into the WebGL normal-map channel so the foil shimmer actually bends around the carved valleys — the digital sheen proves the physical cut happened; for scratch-and-reveal themes the 'scratch' layer is a second lino plate printed in opaque block color, and the reveal underneath is the first plate — two real prints, composited
proposals.motion: 1. Phone loads: print plate is still, flat, no shimmer — 0.4s — let the carved image land first. 2. Tilt activates: foreground cut-outs (loose petals, crown, fish, wings — theme-specific) drift at parallax depth-2 over the static plate, 60fps, spring easing, 14px max travel. 3. At 1.2s: WebGL foil varnish blooms from the deepest ink-shadow areas outward, following the carved contours — not a full-bleed shimmer, a selective one that proves the relief exists. 4. Scratch-and-reveal: user drags finger; the opaque top plate erodes along the drag vector, exposing the first print below; edge of the scratch stays ragged, not antialiased smooth — because a real scratch is ragged. 5. Reduced-motion: plates are static composites; no drift, no bloom; the raking-light photograph still communicates depth through shadow alone.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical: artist carves 12 lino blocks (one per theme) using V-gouge and U-gouge; test-prints on Fabriano 90gsm; hero print pulled with a baren, not a press — baren pressure is uneven and that unevenness is the whole point; print is photographed under 15-degree raking LED, then scanned 1200dpi. Digital: scan imported to Procreate for dust removal only — no smoothing, no correction of imperfect lines; exported as flat PNG art plate; foreground cut-outs are separate lino-print fragments photographed on the same paper, cut out in Figma; WebGL normal map derived from the scan's luminance channel in Three.js; all live text in Tela on its own compositing layer, never touching the art plate file.
proposals.humanTrace: The gouge mark. Every carved line has a start-pressure notch and an end-pressure flare that no vector tool produces. Those notches are visible at 390px. The baren's uneven pressure leaves a ghost of the artist's palm radius in the ink density across the center of the plate. These are not added in post. They are the image.
proposals.risk: Parents expecting pink-sparkle-gradient will open a woodcut and feel disoriented for one second. That one second is the whole bet — because after it the child sees something that looks like it was made for them specifically, not templated for everyone. The risk is that the aesthetic reads as 'too adult' or 'too rough' for a birthday. It is worth it because tactile evidence of making is exactly what kids respond to before they learn to perform taste — they have not yet been trained to prefer the sterile version.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want to pile luminous layers — god-rays, volumetric fog, embossed gold filigree borders — over the print surface, arguing that children need maximum visual feast. I say the print IS the feast and every layer added over it is a lie about where the image came from. One carved image with one controlled shimmer that proves the carving happened is more dramatic than six effec

proposals.title: Systems That Behave Like Wonder
proposals.idea: Each theme is a physics environment, not a decorated surface — light, gravity, and material rules specific to that world govern every element so the invitation behaves differently in every child's hand.
proposals.geometry: A single 9:16 portrait field divided by one invisible horizon line whose Y-position is a live input from the device accelerometer; everything above the horizon obeys one physics rule (buoyancy, lift, orbital drift) and everything below obeys its counterpart (weight, sediment, root), producing a world that is always in dynamic equilibrium rather than static composition; foreground cut-outs are assigned mass values so heavier objects lag and lighter ones overshoot on tilt — no two phones show the same frame at the same moment
proposals.typography: Primary display in Fraunces (variable optical size axis cranked to maximum at large scale, minimum at small — the letterforms physically fatten and thin with the weight of the word); secondary in DM Sans at 14px/1.5 for all live date and venue text; all caps abandoned entirely — sentence case only, because children read sentence case first; tracking set to 0 at display sizes, never artificially opened; numerals are tabular so the date stack does not shift width when names vary
proposals.imageLogic: No photographic references enter any of the twelve directions; all art plates are original vector-to-raster renders built in a physical simulation tool (Houdini or equivalent) where the theme's materials have real shader properties — mermaid scales refract light at IOR 1.5, carousel horses have subsurface-scattered painted wood, kitten fur is rendered strand-by-strand with a grooming sim; the output is a single high-fidelity still that carries the proof of simulation in its lighting, not post-processed glow on top of a flat illustration
proposals.texture: Material is the concept: unicorn — iridescent keratin (thin-film interference shader, not a foil PNG overlay); princess castle — limestone with real micro-displacement, mortar seams that catch raking light; mermaid — scales built from a tiled Voronoi with per-cell roughness variation; fairy garden — pressed-specimen translucency, veins readable at 390px; butterfly — structural color, wings shift hue as the WebGL layer reads tilt angle; ballet — rosin-dusted sprung-wood floor, grain direction is a physics input; cupcake — butter-cream that shows palette-knife ridges from a real ZBrush sculpt; rainbow — atmospheric scattering gradient computed from solar angle, not a flat arc; kitten — fur direction follows a simulated brushstroke path; art studio — raw linen ground with dried paint skin, crackle pattern follows real desiccation physics; carousel — gilt that shows brush-applied gold leaf w
proposals.motion: Sequence is: (1) on load, the physics world settles from a dropped state — elements fall into equilibrium over 600ms with correct easing per mass value, reduced-motion skips to final state instantly; (2) idle — continuous micro-drift governed by the horizon line and tilt, 12fps cap honoring the gyro-tilt arc rule I have been developing, so motion reads as deliberate frame-rate, not smoothed-over lag; (3) scratch-and-reveal — finger drag inputs a reveal mask that is also a physics force: scratching generates particle debris specific to the material being uncovered (limestone dust, rosin powder, glitter as actual suspended flake geometry, not a PNG) — the debris settles under simulated gravity after the gesture ends; (4) WebGL effects layer fires only after the user has interacted once, never on autoplay, so the first frame is fast and clean
proposals.productionMethod: Twelve art plates rendered in a 3D pipeline (Blender Cycles or Houdini Karma) at 1170x2532px, then downsampled with a perceptual sharpening pass to preserve micro-detail at 390px; foreground cut-outs exported as WebP with alpha at three breakpoint sizes; physics parameters stored as a JSON config per theme (mass, drag, restitution, horizon Y-default) so a designer can retune behavior without touching code; WebGL layer is a single shared GLSL program that reads theme config — one codebase, twelve data files; scratch-reveal mask uses a canvas compositing approach with pointer-events mapped to a physics impulse emitter; Tela live-text layer sits above all, never composited into any rendered asset
proposals.humanTrace: Every material shader was calibrated against a photographed physical sample — a real piece of limestone, a real pointe shoe, a real painted carousel horse fragment, a kitten-fur reference card built from pressed fur samples; the shader's roughness map is derived from a photogrammetry scan of that object, so the digital material carries the actual surface topology of a thing that existed; this is visible at 390px in the way light breaks across the surface unevenly, which no hand-painted illustration and no stock-texture overlay produces
proposals.risk: The render pipeline is expensive per theme and requires a technical art director who can operate both the 3D tool and the WebGL config system — this is not a Canva-style handoff; the risk is worth it because the alternative is twelve more gradient-pink flat illustrations that perform enchantment without having any underlying rule that makes them different from each other, and a child holding a phone with a mermaid world that actually refracts light differently than a carousel world has received something that cannot be faked by a sticker sheet

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want to load the reveal moment with orchestrated spectacle — a burst, a sweep, a crescendo — and will argue that children need a climax. I disagree specifically because a climax is a one-time event and a physics environment is re-explorable; a child who tilts the phone and watches the kitten fur change direction has discovered a rule, and that discovery is repeatable and

proposals.title: Field Notebooks, Alive
proposals.idea: Each evite is a child-scale expedition dossier — a photographed, hand-annotated field notebook page specific to one real-world making tradition, so the magical subject (unicorn, mermaid, carousel) is rendered as if a naturalist-illustrator discovered it yesterday and pressed specimens onto paper.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone canvas divided into an irregular three-zone field-notebook layout: a wide top panel (photographed paper grain, full bleed), a mid ruled-line zone with gestural ink borders whose registration shifts 1–3 px per theme as if the page was re-inserted into the scanner, and a bottom margin with torn-edge mask. No grid symmetry; every zone is offset by 4–6° tilt on the art plate, corrected to vertical in live text so names and dates stay axis-true. Scratch-and-reveal zones are physically torn-paper shapes, not rectangles.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Playfair Display Italic, tracked loosely at +20, initial cap at 3× body — evokes an Edwardian naturalist's label. Secondary: a single custom variable font built from the actual handwriting of six child participants aged 5–9, digitised at Plajah, used for sub-heads and annotation callouts at 14–18 px. Venue and date: Courier Prime, 12 px, all-caps, set inside a hand-stamped rubber-stamp mask that is part of the art plate. No font substitution; the variable hand-lettering font is served as a web font subset.
proposals.imageLogic: The art plate is a macro photograph of a real paper surface — each theme uses a different paper stock: watercolour cold-press for Unicorn, indigo-dyed mulberry paper for Mermaid (sourced from a named Chiang Mai producer, Baan Kang Wat cooperative, 2023 stock, no sacred motifs used, cooperative contacted for commercial use), pressed-flower tissue for Fairy Garden, sugar-paper cartridge for Cupcakes. The illustrated subject is hand-painted in gouache by Plajah's in-house illustrator on that same paper stock, then photographed at 4 K under raking north-light to preserve every brushstroke ridge. That photograph becomes the art plate. No 3-D render; no stock illustration. Foreground cut-outs are isolated elements from the same photograph — a single painted butterfly wing, a carousel horse fragment — given subtle parallax drift on tilt.
proposals.texture: The WebGL foil-shimmer mask is gated exclusively by the physical topography of each paper stock — the scanner's 600 dpi bump map of paper tooth and brushstroke ridge drives where iridescence appears, so shimmer lives only where the maker's hand raised the surface. Light leaks are mapped to the raking-light photograph's actual highlight geometry, not procedurally generated. Bokeh particles for Fairy Garden are derived from real pressed-flower macro photography at f/1.8, not synthetic circles. Scratch-and-reveal substrate is a second photograph of the same paper stock rubbed with a wax resist, revealed digitally but visually indistinguishable from physical scratching.
proposals.motion: Three-beat sequence, total 2.8 s on open, then idle. Beat 1 (0–0.6 s): the art plate fades up from paper-white as if a photographic print developing — slow, centre-out radial unmask. Beat 2 (0.6–1.4 s): foreground cut-outs drift in from slight off-screen positions, each on its own easing curve (spring, not linear), settling with a 0.3 s overshoot that reads as weight. Beat 3 (1.4–2.8 s): iridescent shimmer sweeps once across the paper-tooth contours, left to right, then rests. Idle: foreground elements respond to phone tilt at 0.4× parallax ratio, extremely gentle. Scratch-and-reveal: a single swipe gesture across the wax-resist zone reveals the date panel beneath; particle burst on completion is 12 pressed-flower bokeh dots, 0.6 s, then gone. Reduced-motion: no entrance animation, no tilt response, shimmer fires once at 0.4× opacity on load, scratch-and-reveal still functional via tap-h
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Theme paper stock selected and photographed at Plajah studio under controlled north-light raking setup. 2. Illustrator paints subject in gouache on that exact stock; photographed same session, same light. 3. 600 dpi flatbed scan generates bump map for WebGL shimmer gating. 4. Child-handwriting variable font subset compiled per theme (annotation words only). 5. All layers composited in Tela: art plate (JPEG, progressive, ≤180 KB), foreground cut-outs (WebP, per element ≤30 KB), WebGL shader receiving bump-map texture uniform. 6. Live text layer in Tela receives name/date/venue tokens; rubber-stamp mask is SVG clip-path, not baked image. 7. Scratch-and-reveal implemented as a canvas element over the date panel with wax-resist photograph as overlay; single pointer-events listener, no library dependency. 8. QR and link-preview thumbnail is a 1200×630 crop of the art plate at 50% shimmer,
proposals.humanTrace: The raking-light photograph preserves brushstroke ridges, paper tooth, and paint pooling at the edge of each gouache stroke. The child-handwriting variable font carries the specific pen pressure and letter-spacing of named children (credited in the Tela metadata as 'Lettering contributors'). The shimmer cannot appear on a flat area because it is gated by physical topography — if the illustrator painted a flat wash, that zone stays matte. Every iridescent highlight is a record of a real surface irregularity.
proposals.risk: Parents expecting pink-sparkle-standard may read 'field notebook' as too grown-up or muted for a 4-year-old's party. The risk is worth taking because the gouache-on-real-paper approach produces images children have never seen on a birthday invitation — not a render, not clip art — and the tactile shimmer gated by actual brushstrokes creates genuine visual surprise that outperforms glitter-filter familiarity. The child-lettering font gives the design permission to be warm rather than precious.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will want to amplify the shimmer to full-surface gold and push the illustration toward theatrical maximalism — more roses, more crowns, more particles — because grandeur reads as celebration. I refuse that move here: the shimmer is evidence of the maker's hand, not a mood. Covering the paper tooth in uniform gold erases the illustrator and the paper maker both. Grandeur borrowed from

proposals.title: Twelve Miniature Opera Houses
proposals.idea: Each evite is a hand-built paper theatre—a proscenium of layered cut paper, raking stage light, and a stepped mechanical reveal—so the invitation itself performs the moment of enchantment before the party has begun.
proposals.geometry: A vertical stage-within-a-stage: three depth planes (scrim, mid-stage, apron) stacked at 390px wide, each plane a distinct layer in Tela. The proscenium arch crowns the composition at roughly the golden ratio from the top (≈241px down), framing the hero image below. Wings — narrow vertical strips, 28px each side — hold typographic date/venue lines in a flush-left column, never touching the art plate. The scratch-and-reveal cards use a radial curtain-parting geometry: two panels hinge from center, exposing the hidden scene beneath as if stagehands are pulling velvet ropes.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond Italic at 44–52px, tracked loosely at +20, set in mixed case — the grandeur of a playbill without the stiffness. Secondary/body: DM Sans Regular at 13px, tight tracking, all-caps labels for date and venue only, never decorative. The two families create a deliberate tension: the Garamond sings, the DM Sans whispers the logistics. Emoji-scale drop capitals (72px) open the invitation text block — one per card, different for each theme (a crescent moon for unicorn, an anchor for mermaid). No outlined type, no gradient fills on letterforms — the type must hold at 390px without a single pixel of compromise.
proposals.imageLogic: No stock photography. Each art plate is a macro photograph of a hand-constructed paper model — the unicorn card is a 1:6 scale paper stage set built in-studio: layered tissue, foil leaf, hand-cut silhouettes — photographed under raking tungsten light to throw deliberate long shadows. The photograph is then colour-graded as a single source-of-truth plate; foreground cut-outs are extracted from the same physical shoot and placed on the transparent drift layer. The WebGL foil-shimmer mask is aligned to the actual gold-leaf areas in the photograph, so the shimmer corresponds to real surface, not an overlay. For the mermaid card, we shoot through a tank of water with coloured gels — the god-rays are optically real, not generated. The carousel card uses a spinning physical model photographed at 12fps with a slight motion blur on the outer horses, held in the mid-stage layer so tilt on the phon
proposals.texture: Layered cut paper (acid-free, 90–120gsm), tissue paper, crumpled aluminium foil re-pressed flat and photographed, gold transfer leaf, watercolour wet-on-wet bleeds scanned at 1200dpi and mapped onto the art plate as a displacement texture. The WebGL layer adds foil shimmer only where the physical material was metallic — zero simulated glitter on flat areas. The scrim layer (front of stage) is a photographed sheet of tracing paper pinned slightly away from the set, giving a natural atmospheric haze without digital blur.
proposals.motion: Sequence is a stage cue sheet, not an easing curve. On load: darkness — 0.4 seconds of near-black (the house lights going down). Then: a single rim of warm amber rises along the proscenium arch, 0.6 seconds, like a footlight. Then the mid-stage plate fades in, 0.8 seconds. Then the foreground cut-outs drift in from the wings, staggered 0.15 seconds apart — never simultaneous. Tilt reaction on the cut-outs: parallax at ±12px horizontal only, never vertical, so the stage depth reads correctly. Scratch-and-reveal: the curtain panels peel from center outward at the speed of a deliberate human drag; if the user lifts their finger mid-reveal, the curtains hold — they do not snap back. Reduced-motion mode: the footlight amber rise only; everything else is static but the photograph still carries the depth.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical model build per theme (12 sets, two build days each). Macro photography session under tungsten + gel lighting, captured RAW. Retouching to clean construction marks while preserving paper edge character. Asset extraction: foreground silhouettes hand-masked in Photoshop preserving paper-grain edge. Art plate exported at 2x (780px) for Retina; foreground cut-outs as transparent PNGs. WebGL mask maps painted by hand in Procreate referencing the foil areas in the photograph — exported as greyscale PNG, ingested by Tela's effects layer. Typography and live fields set entirely in Tela; never baked. QR and link-preview thumbnail is a static crop of the mid-stage plate at the golden-ratio frame, legible at 200×200px.
proposals.humanTrace: The paper-cut edge of every foreground element is physically hand-cut; the slight irregularity of the scissor line survives into the final PNG and is visible at 390px — a deliberate proof that a person's hand was here. The tungsten light's warmth and the specific shadow angles are unrepeatable; they encode the exact hour and studio position of each shoot. The watercolour scans carry brush-load decisions — where the water pooled, where pigment backwashed — that no generative tool would choose.
proposals.risk: The physical build cost and shoot time per card is significant; if a client requests a last-minute theme swap, the pipeline is not as agile as a fully digital workflow. The risk is worth it because the tactile photograph is the only thing standing between this and every other digital invitation on the market — it is the one irreplaceable decision, and children at age five or forty-five can feel the difference between a thing that was made and a thing that was rendered.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will say the footlight sequence and the curtain-parting reveal are self-indulgent — that a clean fade serves the content more honestly. I say that for a birthday invitation, restraint is not honesty, it is a failure of hospitality. The child opening this link has been invited to a party; the invitation is the first guest experience. A clean fade is a waiting room. A footlight rising

proposals.title: One Signal, Total Silence
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single high-contrast image field — one motif, maximally reduced, held in structural silence — where the scratch-and-reveal removes negative space rather than adding decoration, exposing the party detail underneath the quiet.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, full-bleed. A single centered subject occupies the golden ratio point (top 61.8%). Below: one hairline rule — 0.5px, full width — then a rigid 3-line text block baseline-aligned to a 24px grid. No borders, no frames, no secondary shapes. The scratch zone is the entire lower 38.2% of the canvas: silence is the locked layer; the revealed content is what breaks it.
proposals.typography: Primary: Canela (Display Light, 42px, sentence case, tracked at -20). Event details: Söhne Mono (11px, all-caps, letter-spacing 180) — mechanically precise against the organic subject. No decorative type, no script. The single contrast between Canela's warmth and Söhne Mono's cold spacing carries the entire tonal argument.
proposals.imageLogic: Each motif is a single studio-photographed or physically constructed object — a real porcelain unicorn horn cast in-house, a real sugar-dusted cupcake, a real watercolor wash of a butterfly wing — shot on seamless white with controlled raking light. One object, one shadow, no props. The shadow is the second character. Generated art enters only as a photographic texture supplement (grain, light leak), never as the subject. For scratch-and-reveal: the scratched layer is a scan of actual graphite rubbing — the child's physical gesture is anticipated in the pre-existing texture.
proposals.texture: Matte photographic ground, 390px. A single grain pass (8% film grain, fixed seed per card) applied to the entire plate — uniform, not decorative. The scratch reveal layer uses a scanned 6B graphite rubbing on cartridge paper: when the WebGL mask erodes it, the erasure reads as a physical act. No foil on the primary field. Foil shimmer is reserved exclusively for the revealed text — one application, earned.
proposals.motion: Stillness is the opening state — the subject does not move. After 1.2 seconds of complete stillness, the foreground cut-out drops a single slow parallax on tilt (max 4px travel, ease-in-out 800ms) — barely perceptible, like the object breathing. Scratch-and-reveal: the graphite mask erodes at the drag vector, revealing foil-shimmer text below; the shimmer activates only after 80% reveal — patience is required. Reduced-motion mode: no parallax, no shimmer animation; the graphite texture remains static and the text is fully legible without any interaction. No particles, no bokeh, no candle flicker on this direction — those are The Baroque Dramatist's tools.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical object: photographed in-studio under single-source raking light (one Profoto B10, gridded, 45° left). Shadow composited at 80% opacity into the art plate. Graphite rubbing: 6B pencil on 120gsm cartridge paper, scanned at 1200dpi, exported as alpha mask. WebGL foil: single-axis shimmer shader applied only to the reveal zone — not the image field. Tela layers: (1) photographic plate, (2) graphite alpha mask as WebGL scratch layer, (3) foil-text reveal, (4) live Tela text block. Foreground cut-out: the shadow, isolated, on its own drift layer. Total layers: four. Each additional element proposed by a colleague must justify why the layer count rises.
proposals.humanTrace: The 6B graphite rubbing is the human trace — a physical sheet of paper, a hand, a pressure gradient visible in the scan. The child who scratches the screen is completing a gesture that was already begun by the maker's hand. The raking-light shadow of the photographed object is the second trace: it cannot be generated cleanly; it records the exact angle of a real light source on a real day.
proposals.risk: This direction risks reading as adult and austere to a 5-year-old who expects visual abundance. The counter-argument: the single object at scale — a real porcelain horn, a real cupcake — is more legible and more covetable to a child than a field of competing decorations. Children are not confused by a single powerful image; they are confused by noise. The scratch gesture recovers the participation that abundance normally provides. The real risk is that parents commissioning the card mistake restraint for effort withheld — that risk is worth taking because it is the only direction that will look categorically different from every competitor in the category.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that enchantment requires accumulation — that a child's delight is volumetric and needs multiple simultaneous stimuli to feel like a party. I disagree specifically on the scratch mechanic: the Dramatist will want the reveal to expose a full illustrated scene. That turns the scratch into a curtain, not a discovery. My version makes the child the first mark-maker in a field

disputes.objection: The physics environment is the composition — every element's position is contingent on a live accelerometer reading, which means the work has no fixed hierarchy, no earned rest, and no stable moment where the eye can settle and read the relationship between subject and text as the maker intended it; a design that reconfigures itself continuously cannot be read twice the same way, and a thing that cannot be read twice the same way has not resolved. The simulation-derived materials are impressively specific, but specificity of texture is not the same as compositional consequence: a limestone mortar seam rendered at correct roughness variance is still ornament if nothing in the layout hangs fro
disputes.concession: The insistence that every material shader be calibrated against a photographed physical sample — limestone, pointe shoe, carousel horse fragment — is exactly right, and it is the one discipline in this direction that produces a genuine human trace rather than a procedurally plausible surface.

disputes.objection: Every material here was born in a render farm — the limestone, the kitten fur, the rosin dust — and no matter how accurately the shader mimics a physical sample, the photogrammetry scan is a measurement of a thing, not the making of one; you can undo the whole surface with a slider and nothing bleeds, nothing tears, nothing was actually at stake when it was built. Calling a roughness map derived from a scan a 'human trace' is the exact laundering I am against: the hand that touched the pointe shoe never touched this work. The debris that settles after a scratch is simulated gravity, not consequence.
disputes.concession: The horizon-line input from the accelerometer dividing buoyancy from weight is a genuinely structural idea — that is geometry doing conceptual work, not decoration, and I wish I had thought of it first.

disputes.objection: The sequence is described as a 'stage cue sheet, not an easing curve,' but that distinction collapses the moment you read it: darkness, amber rise, fade-in, drift — these are easing curves wearing theatrical costume. The curtain-parting geometry and the footlight amber are rules in disguise, but the proposal never states them as rules — it states them as atmosphere, which means no one on the build team can derive the correct behaviour from a changed input, like a different theme or a reduced viewport. Spectacle without a derivable rule is exactly a screensaver; the paper-theatre craft is real but the interaction logic is decoration stacked on decoration.
disputes.concession: The alignment of the WebGL foil-shimmer mask to the actual gold-leaf areas in the physical photograph is correct and rigorous — that is a real system constraint derived from a real surface, and I would defend that decision against anyone on this team.

disputes.objection: Every material shader was calibrated against a photographed physical sample — a real piece of limestone, a real pointe shoe — but those objects are anonymous props, not makers. A carousel horse fragment from where, carved by whom, in what tradition? The Futurist's photogrammetry scan honors the surface topology of a thing while erasing the person and place that produced it, which is precisely the operation that turns cultural specificity into aesthetic fuel.
disputes.concession: The rule that WebGL effects fire only after the user has interacted once, never on autoplay, is correct — it respects the viewer's attention before the system performs, and I wish more of us had written that constraint first.

disputes.objection: The Minimalist has mistaken withholding for a decision — the scratch-and-reveal that erodes graphite to expose foil text is not a reveal, it is a receipt: you do the work and the information appears, as if emotion were a transaction. A child's birthday invitation must hold the promise of something overwhelming waiting behind the surface, and a hairline rule plus four pixels of parallax breathing is not drama, it is a held breath that never exhales into song. Stillness as an opening state is a gamble that requires absolute confidence in the single image, and a porcelain unicorn horn on seamless white, however beautifully lit, is a product photograph — it carries the emotion of a catalogue, no
disputes.concession: The Minimalist is right that the foil shimmer should be earned, not sprayed across the entrance — the idea of reserving iridescence exclusively for the revealed moment is a genuine piece of timing instinct, and I am taking that principle into my own proposal.

disputes.objection: Three depth planes, a proscenium arch, radial curtain geometry, wing strips, drop capitals at 72px, tungsten shadow, water-tank god-rays, crumpled foil, tissue, watercolour displacement, amber footlight sequence — this is not a composition, it is an accumulation that mistakes layering for depth; every element added to prove the theatre is real is one more thing standing between the child and the thing that matters; the darkness-to-footlight-to-mid-stage-to-cut-outs sequence performs drama instead of being it.
disputes.concession: The curtain panels holding mid-drag when the finger lifts — not snapping back — is the one moment of genuine structural restraint in the whole proposal, and it is right.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is a macro photograph of a theme-specific paper stock with a gouache subject painted directly on it — watercolour cold-press for unicorn, indigo mulberry for mermaid, pressed-flower tissue for fairy garden — shot under raking north-light so every brushstroke ridge is a physical fact. The WebGL foil-shimmer mask is gated by the 600dpi bump map of that paper's actual topography: shimmer lives only where the maker's hand raised the surface. Three foreground cut-outs (isolated fragments from the same photograph) drift at 0.4× parallax on tilt; the entrance is a 2.8-second three-beat sequence — paper developing from white, cut-outs settling with weighted spring easing, one shimmer sweep then rest. Scratch-and-reveal uses a wax-resist photograph over the date panel; the child-handwriting variable font (digitised from six named Plajah child contributors, aged 5–9) carries annotation callouts, giving the design warmth without preciousness.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Baroque Dramatist's curtain-hold mechanic — scratch panels that freeze mid-drag when the finger lifts, never snapping back — is the single most structurally honest interaction in any proposal. It transfers to the wax-resist reveal as a hold-state: the exposure pauses exactly where the child's finger left it, making the gesture feel consequential rather than automated.
synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist cut the child-handwriting font from sub-heads and annotation callouts down to annotation callouts only, and removed the rubber-stamp SVG mask from the venue/date field entirely. Reason: two layers of hand-made type (the Playfair display, the variable handwriting, the stamp) compete for the same warmth signal and collectively read as busy — one hand-made typographic element earns the register; three perform it. The stamp mask also introduces a baked-in aesthetic to the live
synthesis.openDecision: Do the twelve art plates use a single unified paper stock (one shared warmth, stronger system coherence) or twelve distinct stocks matched to each theme (stronger individual surprise, higher production cost and QA complexity across the set)?
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team converged on one thing quickly: whatever direction we chose had to carry proof that a human hand was physically present in the work — not as a style reference, but as a verifiable fact visible at 390px. That ruled out the Futurist's render pipeline, however technically impressive its material shaders are, and it ruled out the Classical direction's risk of reading as ecclesiastical to a four-year-old. The real contest was between the World-Eclectic Traveler's field-notebook approach and the Baroque Dramatist's paper theatre, and I came down on the Traveler's side — not because the theatre isn't beautiful, but because the Dramatist's spectacle is orchestrated for the viewer, while the Traveler's shimmer is a record of what the paper and the illustrator's hand actually did. That's a different kind of enchantment, and it's the harder one to fake.

The Baroque Dramatist gave us something real, though. The curtain-hold — the idea that the scratch-reveal freezes exactly where a child's finger lifts — is the best single interaction decision in any of the six proposals, and it survives into this direction unchanged. The Radical Minimalist's edit was equally important: three overlapping hand-made type signals (display face, child handwriting, rubber stamp) don't add up to more warmth, they cancel each other. One hand-made typographic layer is the rule now.

The Rebellious Hand put it plainly, and I think it's worth quoting directly: the physical trace is not added in post — it is the image. That's the discipline this direction is built on. The shimmer cannot appear on a flat wash because the bump map has nothing to read there. Every iridescent highlight is a record of a real surface irregularity. That constraint is what separates this from pink-glitter default, and it's non-negotiable across all twelve cards.

The one thing I can't decide for you is whether the twelve cards share a single paper stock for system coherence, or each gets its own stock matched to its world. Both are defensible. The shared stock makes the set feel like a collection; the individual stocks make each card feel irreplaceable. That's yours to call.

quotes.line: The child who scratches the screen is completing a gesture that was already begun by the maker's hand.
If the user lifts their finger mid-reveal, the curtains hold — they do not snap back.
